q: 1. Fire bricks should be laid in a
explain: To maintain thermal consistency, fire bricks are laid using fire clay mortar which can resist similar high temperatures.

q: 2. The bricks used for lining of furnaces are
explain: Refractory bricks, made to withstand very high temperatures, are used to line furnaces.

q: 3. In bricks masonry, the frog of the brick generally kept on
explain: The 'frog' (indentation) is placed facing up so that it can be filled with mortar, creating a mechanical key with the course above.

q: 4. If iron oxide present in brick earth is more than the requirement then colour of the brick after burning will be
explain: Excess iron oxide oxidizes further during burning, deepening the red color of the fired brick.

q: 5. Bull nose bricks are not used in
explain: Bullnose bricks have rounded edges and are used for corners or pillars, but they are not standard for arch construction.

q: 6. Hollow bricks are used for
explain: The air trapped inside hollow bricks acts as an excellent thermal insulator, keeping interiors cooler in summer and warmer in winter.

q: 7. Fire bricks are used
explain: Refractory bricks have low thermal conductivity, helping to contain heat within a furnace and decrease outward heat flow.

q: 8. Terracotta is used in building for
explain: Terracotta is a glazed or unglazed fired clay used primarily for decorative architectural elements and ornamental work.

q: 9. Bloating of bricks is due to
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter and sulphur
presence of any gas forming material in clay
explain: Bloating is a spongy swollen mass caused by the entrapped gases from carbonaceous matter and sulphur during firing.

q: 10. Swelling of bricks is known as
explain: Bloating is the term for the permanent swelling of a brick, often caused by internal gas pressure during burning.

q: 11. The quantity of sand in brick is about
explain: Silica (sand) typically makes up about 50-60% of brick earth, which is roughly equivalent to 3/5ths.

q: 12. The bricks are properly soaked in water before use the following reason
options: to wash the kiln dust for better bondage with mortar
to avoid the chances of absorption of water from the mortar
to spread the mortar uniformly between them
explain: Soaking ensures the bricks don't suck water from the mortar (which weakens it) and removes dust for better adhesion.

q: 13. In one day, the height of brick masonry construction should generally not exceed
explain: To prevent the fresh mortar in lower courses from being crushed by the weight of new work, the daily height is limited to 1m.

q: 14. Frog means
explain: In masonry terminology, a frog is the depression or indentation made on the top face of a brick.

q: 15. For manufacture of bricks normally the top soil is removed having a depth of .....
explain: The top 20cm of soil is usually stripped away (unsoiling) as it contains organic matter and impurities unsuitable for bricks.

q: 16. Tampering of soil for manufacture of bricks, is done by
explain: Kneading the soil (tempering) can be done manually by feet, using cattle, or mechanically in a pug mill.

q: 17. In case of clamp for burning of bricks, the bricks/ fuel are laid at a slope of...
explain: Clamps are constructed with a slight inward slope, usually around 15 degrees, to ensure stability as the fuel burns away.

q: 18. Normally the bricks (1st class) obtained from pazawah is about
explain: Pazawah (clamp) burning is less efficient than kiln burning, typically yielding about 60% good quality bricks.

q: 19. Terracotta, in building, is used for
explain: Terracotta, a fired clay product, is commonly used for decorative and ornamental architectural work.

q: 20. Lamination of bricks is caused due to
options: entrapped air in the voids of the clay
entrapped water in the voids of the clay
explain: Lamination occurs when air is trapped within the clay during machine moulding, creating thin layers or planes of weakness.

q: 21. Strike is used to remove the
explain: A strike is a wooden or metal straight-edge used to scrape off excess clay from the top of the mould.

q: 22. Refractory bricks are used in
explain: Refractory bricks are essential for lining combustion chambers where temperatures are extremely high.

q: 23. Refractory bricks are
explain: Refractory bricks are categorized into three types—acidic, basic, and neutral—based on their chemical resistance to slag.

q: 24. Generally wooden moulds are made from
explain: Hardwoods like Shisham are preferred for brick moulds because they resist wear and warping from moisture.

q: 25. Choose the correct statement
options: percentage of silica is increased in 1st class brick
percentage of alumina is increased in refractory brick
percentage of alumina is increased in 1st class brick
explain: Refractory bricks require a higher percentage of alumina (and silica) to withstand extreme temperatures without melting.

q: 26. If rain water falls on hot bricks then the shape of the brick gets deformed, this defect is known as
explain: Chuffs is the defect caused when falling rain hits hot, newly burnt bricks, resulting in cracking and deformation.

q: 27. The discolouration and formation of white deposits due to presence of relatively large proportion of soluble salts in a bricks is known as
explain: Efflorescence is the white powdery deposit left on a brick surface when moisture evaporates and leaves behind soluble salts.

q: 28. Dolomite bricks are
explain: Dolomite is a basic material; therefore, bricks made from it are classified as basic refractory bricks.

q: 29. Jhumb bricks
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks that have become vitrified and often distorted in shape.

q: 30. Second class bricks
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: While 2nd class bricks may have slight irregularities, they should still be well-burnt and produce a metallic ringing sound.

q: 31. The reason for the popularity of bricks as construction material is that
options: they are cheap and available locally at all places
they are durable and possess fairly good strength and lighter than stones
they have very good insulating property against heat and sound
explain: Bricks are widely used due to their cost-effectiveness, durability, ease of handling, and natural insulation properties.

q: 32. The most widely used kiln in Nepal is
explain: Bull's Trench Kiln is the most popular type in Nepal due to its cost-efficiency and ability to produce a large volume of bricks continuously.

q: 33. The standard size of brick as per Indian standard is
explain: The standard modular brick size as per IS: 1077 is 19 cm x 9 cm x 9 cm.

q: 34. The soil used for the manufacture of bricks should preferably not contain the following material
explain: Alkalies cause efflorescence, while pebbles and kankar lead to cracking and weakness in the finished brick.

q: 35. Which of the following ingredients of brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica provides the structural bulk and rigidity that helps the brick retain its shape after molding and firing.

q: 36. Advantage of a clamp compared to a kiln for burning bricks is that
options: it takes less time for burning
it gives more output of first class bricks
it is suitable when bricks are required in large numbers
explain: A clamp requires far less capital investment to set up compared to a permanent kiln structure.

q: 37. Efflorescence is caused if
options: the alkaline salt is present in the bricks
the clay used for making bricks contain pyrite
the water used for pugging the clay contains gypsum
explain: Efflorescence can arise from multiple sources of soluble salts — alkalies in the clay, pyrite, or gypsum-contaminated water — all of which crystallize on the surface.

q: 38. The frog of a brick is normally made on its
explain: The frog is pressed into the top (frog) face of the brick during molding, which also helps key it to the mortar above.

q: 39. The maximum percentages of warping along the sides of tiles, is
explain: Quality control standards for tiles generally allow for a maximum of 2% warping along the edges.

q: 40. The thermal conductivity of glass is
explain: Glass has low thermal conductivity, making it a relatively poor conductor of heat.

q: 41. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: equal to the size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of a fully burnt brick
greater than the size of a fully burnt brick
explain: The mould is made larger than the final brick size to account for shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 42. Advantage of a clamp compared to a kiln for burning bricks is that
options: it takes less time for burning
it gives more output of first class bricks
it is suitable when bricks are required in large numbers
explain: A clamp is a temporary, simple structure requiring far less capital investment than a permanent kiln.

q: 43. The strength of a brick decreases by about ........ percent when soaked in water
explain: Water absorption weakens the internal bond structure of a brick, reducing its strength by about 25% when soaked.

q: 44. If the water absorption of bricks is 5% of its weight, the brick may be
explain: A very low water absorption of 5% indicates a dense, high-quality brick, typical of heavy duty machine-made bricks.

q: 45. The colour of fire bricks is generally
explain: Fire bricks, made from fire clay low in iron oxide, typically fire to a yellowish-white color.

q: 46. Efflorescence in bricks is caused by
options: the high pH content of water used during pugging
low silica content of the bricks
explain: Efflorescence results from soluble alkaline salts within the brick migrating to the surface and crystallizing as water evaporates.

q: 47. Percentage of silica in a good brick earth lies between
explain: Silica forms the bulk of good brick earth, typically comprising about 50 to 60%.

q: 48. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the thickness of wall is
explain: Since stretcher bond shows only the long face of bricks, it is suitable only for half-brick-thick (9 cm) walls.

q: 49. Which of the following pairs gives a correct combination of the useful and harmful constituents respectively of a good brick earth?
explain: Silica is a useful (structural) constituent of brick earth, while alkalies are harmful, causing efflorescence.

q: 50. Number of brick required for one cubic meter of brick masonry is ( as per IS)
explain: As per this reference (IS), about 500 bricks are typically required per cubic meter of brick masonry.
